clue.text: California policeman starts to head off New York racket

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
a cop is an informal word for a police officer

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these two words
NY is the standard abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A Californian officer is told to leave for New York, where some shady scheme is running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a criminal scheme to match the policeman, but it means noise; 'head off' reads as an instruction to set out, not as two words whose first letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud unpleasant din, and a cacophony is a harsh jarring mixture of sounds.

clue.text: Organise minister

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to select and arrange items, as for an exhibition
second meaning: an assistant member of the clergy in a parish

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an order to arrange a minister's affairs, but the verb and the clergyman are two separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means selecting and arranging exhibits; as a noun it names a junior parish priest, a kind of church official.

clue.text: Nicks French fries

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small cuts or notches knocked out of a surface
second meaning: the British word for deep-fried potato strips

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like someone stealing French fries, with 'Nicks' as the British slang for steals; in fact it is the noun for small notches. In Britain fries are called chips.
explanation.definitionFit: Small notches knocked out of china are this, and the British also use the word for fried potato strips served with fish.

clue.text: In favour of bold leader of your quality

parts.note: pro means for, in support of
pert means cheeky or forward

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only that opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone backs a confident leader because of the personal quality they show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold leader' seems a phrase about a brave chief, but 'bold' gives a word for cheeky and 'leader' works on the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A property is an attribute or characteristic of something, as in the healing properties of a plant.

clue.text: Continue a poem after rewriting opening phrase

indicators.note: rewriting something sets it down again in a new form, so these letters are put into a different order

parts.note: the thirteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A writer is told to carry on with a poem once they have reworked how it begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sits neatly in the world of writing, which hides that the first three words are simply letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional formula with which fairy tales and children's stories begin.

clue.text: Mournful cry of Yangtze's apex predator

indicators.note: in a down clue the apex of a word is its topmost letter, which is the first

parts.note: the first letter of the river's name, its top in a down clue
an owl is a bird that hunts prey

explanation.surface: The top predator of the Yangtze river lets out a sorrowful howl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apex predator' is a familiar ecological phrase, but here it splits: 'apex' picks out the top of the river's name and the predator is a hunting bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A yowl is a long loud wailing howl, as of a cat or a person in distress.

clue.text: Objective conclusion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an aim or goal
second meaning: the final part of something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like an adjective meaning impartial, describing the conclusion, but it is the noun for a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a purpose aimed at and also the finishing point or last section of anything.

clue.text: Empty engine part

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to use up completely, as a verb
second meaning: the pipe expelling waste gases from a motor

explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' looks like an adjective describing a hollow engine part, but it is a verb meaning to drain completely.
explanation.definitionFit: To use up supplies fully is one sense; the other is the system carrying spent gases away from a car motor.

clue.text: Shirker embarrassed about swallowing overdose by end of evening

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word is written backwards
what is swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
OD is the standard abbreviation for overdose

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that last letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A shirker is mortified at having taken an overdose late in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The embarrassment word is written backwards, then opened up to take the overdose abbreviation followed by the last letter of 'evening': D(OD G)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodger is someone who evades duties or obligations, as in a tax dodger or draft dodger.

clue.text: Animal horn I processed

indicators.note: material that has been processed is broken down and reworked, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the five letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to having processed an animal's horn, evoking the illegal trade in ivory and horn.
explanation.walkthrough: The horn and the answer belong together, since this beast is poached for exactly that horn; the word is simply rearranged with the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhino, short for rhinoceros, is a large thick-skinned African or Asian mammal, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Intimidates man beginning to demolish farm building

parts.note: to cow someone is to frighten them into submission
he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, which is the one kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: A bully frightens a man into starting to knock down a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimidates' seems a plain verb in the story, but the word for it doubles as the plural of a farm animal, which fits the building neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed is a shelter on a farm where cattle are housed or milked.

clue.text: Refined fuel sat undergoing changes after time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: something undergoing changes is being altered, so these letters are moved into a new arrangement

parts.note: the seven letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Refined fuel has been sitting in storage, changing chemically as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refined fuel' reads as one phrase about petroleum, but 'Refined' alone is the definition; the time abbreviation goes in front of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe good judgement in style and manners, showing elegance and a sense of what is fitting.

clue.text: Ineffective European bloke

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is British slang for an ordinary man, and the answer is its American counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a man or guy, one British and one American in flavour.

clue.text: Mark about to get part

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a member is a part of a body or structure

explanation.surface: Mark is just about to land a role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name about to get a part in a show, but it is the verb used in 'mark the anniversary'.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark an occasion is to commemorate it, which is to honour and recall it in memory.

clue.text: Outgoing former partner right to keep collection of valuables

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a trove is a store of treasure
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sociable ex claims the right to retain the jewellery collection after the split.
explanation.walkthrough: The ex and the right abbreviation together surround the treasure: EX(TROVE)RT. 'Outgoing' looks like it describes a departing partner, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective outgoing describes someone sociable and confident, and the noun names such a sociable person; a slight shift of part of speech.

clue.text: Devious first lady accepting travel permit in retrospect

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the word is read from the end to the start
accepting something means taking it in, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible
a visa allows entry to a country

explanation.surface: Looking back, the president's wife was shifty about granting someone a visa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the first woman of Genesis; the permit is turned round and slipped inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devious avoids straight answers and is shifty, which is what being evasive means.

clue.text: Remaining unaccustomed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: left over and not taken up
second meaning: not familiar with something

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: spare stock left over, and a person not yet used to something; the second is pronounced with a soft s.
explanation.definitionFit: Items left over have not been taken up, and someone not familiar with a situation is described with the same word.

clue.text: Knocked down clerk's case in action

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word, ignoring the possessive

explanation.surface: A clerk's legal case is caught up in a lawsuit and gets thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'action' both look like legal terms; in fact one picks the outside letters and the other is a synonym for an act. 'Decked' is informal for punched to the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck someone is slang for punching them so they fall to the ground, which is knocking them down.

clue.text: Old lady consuming a bread product

indicators.note: consuming means eating, taking something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly woman eats some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Nan is the British informal word for a grandmother, a common reading of 'old lady'.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, baked in a tandoor oven.

clue.text: Carefully observe reserved books by head of education

parts.note: a reserved seat is taken
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone is told to watch closely the books held on reserve by the head of the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' is a classic crossword trap: it gives the Old Testament abbreviation rather than a word for volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To take note is to pay attention and register something mentally, which means watching it attentively.

clue.text: Have one's home under old tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, being beneath means coming lower in the column, so the residence piece is placed second

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for old
to live somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: Someone makes their home beneath an ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places the first piece below the second, so the residence word sits beneath the old abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is an evergreen Mediterranean tree grown for its small oily fruit.

clue.text: Swear leaders of community undertaking suck sometimes

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters, so the first letter of each is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words

explanation.surface: Community leaders admit their joint projects are sometimes so bad they make you swear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of community' seems to mean local officials, but it picks out the first letter of each of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuss is an informal variant of curse, meaning to use bad language or swear.

clue.text: Incentives limit US supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, this means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Economic incentives will restrict the American money supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun, as in money supply, but it is read as 'supple-y', an adverb meaning in a pliant way.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that spur action or growth, as with economic stimulus packages, so they act as incentives.

clue.text: Black hazard is sharp

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a risk is a hazard or danger

explanation.surface: A warning that black ice is a sharp danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black hazard' reads as a single danger such as black ice, but the colour gives only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk wind or manner is keen and cutting, and sharp air is cold and bracing in the same way.

clue.text: Scheduled fitting

definitions.meaning: first meaning: expected at a set time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scheduled fitting' sounds like an appointment with a tailor, but the two words are separate meanings of one short adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Expected at an appointed time is one sense; owed as right and proper, as in due care, is the other.

clue.text: Vanguard he parades around

indicators.note: moved around means scattered here and there, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the nine letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: A man marches about at the front of the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The military parade fits the vanguard so well that 'parades' reads as a verb rather than letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A vanguard is the leading part of an army or movement, and a spearhead is the force leading an attack.
